scope: Proposition 2.6 (Arbitrary auxiliary weights) of the manuscript “Endpoint pointwise convergence for the Schrodinger equation in higher dimensions” (preprints/Endpoint-pointwise-convergence-for-the-Schrodinger-equation-in-higher-dimensions-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 080 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f859efa28f227ff), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let 2 < p ≤ qk, and let fT be band-limited packets of scale N. For bT ≥ 0, require fT = 0 if bT = 0, and set Bb(z)2 = P T b2 T wT (z). Then, for every ε > 0, Z Bb(z)2−p X T fT (z) p dz ≤ CεNε Nk+2 X T sp T b2−p T . (2.15) The integrand is defined as zero where both the field and Bb vanish. The estimate admits unit suprema. If all frequency labels lie within C/N of a κ-dimensional affine plane, 1 ≤ κ ≤ k, the range extends to 2 < p ≤ qκ. In the zero-dimensional case there are only boundedly many frequency slots and the assertion holds for every fixed finite p > 2.
